query_text: A specialist referral network app where freelance consultants can list their niche expertise and get recommended to clients who need someone outside their own skill set — kind of like a mutual referral club for independent professionals, all in a browser-based tool you can use from your desk, with a simple directory of consultants organized by specialty so you can browse who's available, and a way to leave a quick note when you're passing along a recommendation to a colleague.

A freelance income tracker that finally stops me from losing track of which clients owe me money and whether I'm actually making a profit after all my expenses — a web app where I can log payments coming in and costs going out for each project, and it automatically shows me my profit margin so I don't have to open a spreadsheet and do the math myself every time I want to know if this month was worth it.

A pricing tool for freelancers that saves all the back-and-forth of typing out quotes from scratch every single time a new client asks — a web app where I can set up my service packages with their prices upfront, then just pick and combine what the client needs and send them a quote instantly without having to recalculate everything manually or dig through old emails to remember what I charged last time.

Create a freelance workload planner that stops me from accidentally saying yes to too many projects at once — a web app for desktop browsers where I can block out which weeks I'm fully booked and which ones I still have room, so when a new client asks if I'm available I can actually check instead of guessing, with a simple calendar view that shows my current projects laid out by timeline and lets me mark days as open or unavailable.

Need a bio generator tool for consultants that takes the pain out of writing about yourself — a browser-based tool where I fill in my specialty, years of experience, and a few things I'm known for, and it spits out a polished professional bio plus a short tagline I can actually use on my website or LinkedIn, with a few different versions to pick from so I'm not stuck staring at a blank page trying to make myself sound impressive.

A portrait photography studio website where potential clients can scroll through sample photos grouped by session type — like family portraits, headshots, maternity — and then see clearly what each shooting package includes and how much it costs, so they can figure out what they want before even reaching out, all in a clean web app that works well in a desktop browser and makes it easy to see the price breakdown for each package at a glance.

Need a tailor shop website that shows off all the different fabrics available with close-up swatch photos people can browse through, plus a gallery of finished custom pieces so customers can see what the end result actually looks like before they come in — a web app for desktop browsers where the fabric options are organized by type or color and each finished outfit photo has a note about what fabric it used, so clients can point to exactly what they want when they book their fitting.

Need a little website for an independent bookshop that shows off the staff picks and curated reading lists so customers know what's worth picking up, plus an upcoming events calendar so people don't miss author talks or book club nights — a web app for desktop browsers where the book collection is browseable by mood or genre and each event has all the details you'd need to decide whether to show up.

An escape room venue website where visitors can browse each room's theme and story before they book — like a preview of the atmosphere, difficulty level, and vibe of each room with a bunch of moody photos so you actually know what you're walking into — a web app for desktop browsers where all the rooms are laid out as a gallery and clicking into one gives you the full picture of what the experience is like, the capacity, and how scary or puzzle-heavy it is.

Build a newsletter site for a local tutoring center that feels warm and encouraging — like flipping through a scrapbook of kids' wins — where each story has a student's photo, a little blurb about what they struggled with and how they turned it around, and the whole thing has that cozy, handwritten-notes-on-the-fridge energy rather than a corporate press release vibe, all as a web app that looks great in a desktop browser with stories flowing in a gentle, readable layout that parents actually want to read.

Need a website for a small catering company that has this lush, seasonal energy — where each new menu gets its own gorgeous reveal with food photography that makes you hungry just looking at it, and past events are recapped with behind-the-scenes photos and little stories about the occasion — a web app that feels editorial and tasteful in a desktop browser, almost like a food magazine, so clients get excited about hiring them before they even make contact.

Need a website for a neighborhood gym that puts real member transformation stories front and center — the kind where you see a before-and-after with a genuine personal quote and it actually feels inspiring rather than cheesy — a web app for desktop browsers where each spotlight has a photo, a short personal story, and maybe the member's favorite class or trainer, giving the whole thing a community feel that makes new people think "that could be me."

A blog-style website for a local cleaning service that shares genuinely useful eco-friendly cleaning tips and honest reviews of green products they actually use — the kind of content that feels like advice from a knowledgeable neighbor rather than an ad — a web app for desktop browsers where each post has a clean, readable layout with good photos and is organized by room type or product category so people can find what they need quickly.

Need a web app for a massage parlor that handles the whole membership upgrade pitch so the staff doesn't have to awkwardly bring it up at checkout — a simple page where customers can see the different membership tiers side by side with what each one includes, the price difference, and a clear upgrade button, all laid out in a desktop browser so the front desk can just pull it up and hand over the keyboard when someone seems interested.

Make a photography studio promotional website that shows off the portrait packages in a way that actually makes people want to book — a web app for desktop browsers where you can see sample photos from each package, exactly what's included like number of looks and edited photos, and the price all in one place, so potential clients stop asking the same questions over email and just pick a package and book.

Need a web app for a coffee shop that replaces those paper punch cards that always get lost or forgotten at home — a digital loyalty tracker where customers can pull it up in a browser, see how many coffees they've bought toward their free one, and the shop owner can look up any customer's count when they come in, with a simple ten-stamps-get-one system that's actually easy to use at the counter.

A yoga studio new member welcome page that lays out exactly what discount they're getting and for how long, so new students feel like they landed somewhere that values them — a web app for desktop browsers with the welcome offer clearly front and center, a quick overview of what class types are available, and a simple way to claim the discount or sign up, so there's no confusion about what the deal is or how to get started.

Build a web app for small craft makers and artisan shops where wholesale buyers can browse what's available, fill out a custom inquiry form with quantities and specs, and get a quote back without anyone having to play phone tag — a browser-based tool for desktop where each product has its bulk pricing tiers listed, and incoming inquiries show up in a simple list on the seller's side so they can respond and track whether quotes got accepted or are still pending.

A tip calculator website for restaurant owners and managers that stops the end-of-shift confusion about who gets what — a web app for desktop browsers where you enter the total tips collected for the shift, add everyone who worked and how many hours each person worked, and it instantly shows how much each staff member takes home, with a way to adjust the split if certain roles get a different percentage, so there are no arguments and the math is always right.

Need a booking website for a photography studio where clients can see the available session packages, pick which one they want with the add-ons that fit their needs like extra outfit changes or rush delivery, and then choose a date and time from a live calendar — a web app for desktop browsers that handles the whole thing from package selection to confirmed booking so I'm not going back and forth over email just to schedule a shoot.

A sales comparison website for people running multiple small franchise locations where you can punch in the revenue numbers for each outlet and instantly see them stacked up side by side — a web app for desktop browsers where the comparison shows this month versus last month for each location, highlights which store is doing best, and keeps a running history so you can actually spot if one location is falling behind without digging through separate spreadsheets.

Need a booking website for a small tailor shop where customers can pick a time to come in for a fitting and say what kind of garment they're getting made — a web app for desktop browsers with a simple calendar showing which time slots are open, a short form to describe the job like whether it's a suit or alterations, and a confirmation that both the tailor and the customer get so nobody shows up by surprise.

Make a personal trainer booking website where clients can see the trainer's available one-on-one time slots for the week and book a session directly — a web app for desktop browsers where you can pick a session length, choose your preferred time from what's open on the calendar, and fill in a quick note about your fitness goals so the trainer knows what to prep for, with the booking going straight into the trainer's schedule without any phone calls.

Need a reservation website for a neighborhood car wash where customers can pick which bay they want and book a specific time slot so there's no line when they show up — a web app for desktop browsers where you can see which bays are open at what times, choose your slot, and get a confirmation with your bay number, and the car wash owner can check the day's schedule at a glance to see how full each bay is.

Need a website for a small vet clinic where pet owners can book a visit without having to call during busy hours and sit on hold — a web app for desktop browsers where you pick your pet type, describe what the visit is for like a checkup or a specific concern, choose a date and open time slot, and get a confirmation email, so both the owner and the clinic know exactly what's coming in and when.
